title: Butter vs. Olive Oil: Fat, Calories, and Key Differences

seo.title: Butter vs. Olive Oil: Fat, Calories, and Differences
seo.meta_description: A tablespoon of butter has about 102 calories and 7 g saturated fat; olive oil about 119 calories and 2 g saturated fat, with far more monounsaturated fat.
seo.search_intent: Compare butter and olive oil for calories, saturated fat, monounsaturated fat, and cooking use.

excerpt: Olive oil is slightly higher in calories by tablespoon because it is essentially all fat, while butter contains water. Their fatty-acid profiles differ much more: a tablespoon of butter has about 7 g saturated fat, compared with roughly 2 g in olive oil, where monounsaturated oleic acid dominates.
content_html:
Butter and olive oil are both cooking fats, but they are not nutritionally interchangeable. The biggest difference is not whether they contain fat—it is which fats dominate and how much water is present.

Per-tablespoon comparison

Butter ~14 gOlive oil ~13.5 g
Calories~102~119
Total fat~11.5 g~13.5 g
Saturated fat~7.3 g~1.9 g
Monounsaturated fat~3 g~10 g

Olive oil is more calorie-dense because it is almost pure fat. Butter contains roughly 15–18% water.

The fatty-acid profile is where they separate

Butter is rich in saturated fat. Olive oil is dominated by oleic acid, a monounsaturated fat. U.S. heart-health guidance generally recommends replacing some saturated fat with unsaturated fats rather than simply adding more total fat.

Butter is not “forbidden”

A nutrition comparison does not require turning one food into poison and the other into medicine. Amount and frequency matter. Butter can fit in a diet, while olive oil generally offers a more favorable fatty-acid profile when used as a routine cooking fat.

They behave differently in cooking

Butter contains milk solids that brown and create flavor but can burn at higher heat. Olive oil lacks those solids and works across dressings, sautéing, roasting, and many frying applications.

Calories are fairly close per spoonful; saturated versus unsaturated fat is the more meaningful nutritional difference.

faq.question: Which has more calories, butter or olive oil?
faq.answer: Olive oil usually has slightly more per tablespoon, about 119 versus 102 calories, because it is nearly pure fat.

faq.question: Which has more saturated fat?
faq.answer: Butter, at roughly 7 g per tablespoon versus about 2 g in olive oil.

faq.question: Can you cook with olive oil?
faq.answer: Yes. It works for dressings, sautéing, roasting, and many frying uses when temperature is controlled appropriately.
